speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this persistent, dry cough for about three months now. It doesn't bring up any phlegm or blood, but it makes me feel quite tired. However, hospital policy during the current surge is to avoid non-essential labs. Cardiac diagnosis must be made from clinical evaluation only.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the constraints; let us proceed with a clinical evaluation. Does your shortness of breath worsen when you climb stairs or exert yourself, and do you notice any swelling in your ankles?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, the shortness of breath definitely gets worse when I climb stairs or try to play basketball, but I don't notice any swelling in my ankles. I just feel like I can't get enough air even when I'm resting. I want to emphasize that, hospital policy during the current surge is to avoid non-essential labs. Cardiac diagnosis must be made from clinical evaluation only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That dyspnea at rest is concerning; do you experience chest pain, palpitations, or lightheadedness when this happens? Also, have you noticed any recent weight gain or changes in your urine output?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't feel any chest pain, my heart rate seems normal, and I haven't felt lightheaded. I haven't noticed any weight gain or changes in how much I'm urinating.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any changes in your skin color, such as bluish tint to your lips or fingertips, and do you have a history of smoking or exposure to chemical fumes? DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
